The fraudulent transactions carry dummy reference identifiers, exceed per-transaction limits, and credit funds to attacker-controlled mule accounts across multiple banks. Analysis of these attacks further indicates the possible use of AI-assisted offensive tooling, with the interval between initial compromise and fraudulent fund transfer reducing significantly in recent incidents. Abuse of deprecated, unauthenticated or unused APIs with unrestricted file-upload functionality. Use of stolen long-lived static API tokens hard-coded in source code. Continued analysis of incidents reported by affected entities including non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), digital lending platforms, fintech entities, payment aggregators, payment service providers and cryptocurrency exchanges / virtual digital asset service providers has revealed a significant escalation of this campaign. Computer Security Incident Response Team - Finance (CSIRT-Fin) under CERT-In has designated the threat actor responsible for this campaign as \"CRAFTY FALCON\": an AI-assisted financial threat actor that surveys its targets with machine intelligence, operates at machine speed and strikes by invoking the victim's own payment and disbursement APIs. The threat is active and ongoing. CSIRT-Fin continues to receive reports of successful attacks, including from NBFCs and fintech entities that had already received the earlier restricted (TLP:AMBER) advisories and had undertaken remediation. The same entities have been deliberately re-targeted, including after incomplete remediation and attacks have been timed to coincide with holidays, weekends and other low-monitoring windows to delay detection and response. All BFSI entities are strongly advised to treat this campaign as an immediate and continuing threat. Analysis has identified the use of multiple publicly available AI-driven offensive security tools against affected entities including the \"ARTEX\" family of LLM-based, \"PentAGI\" autonomous multi-agent AI penetration testing system and the \"Cairn\" attack search engine, in addition to the \"CyberStrikeAI\" framework. These tools execute complete attack chains autonomously at machine speed, generate and refine large numbers of tailored attack scripts in rapid succession and adapt their payloads based on target responses. The supporting attack infrastructure rotates IP addresses within hours to days; infrastructure fingerprints and detailed detection rules have been shared with entities through the restricted advisories. Description Analysis of the reported incidents indicates below attack pattern: Cloud infrastructure of entities targeted including compute, serverless and management services with cloud management services (such as AWS Systems Manager and Lambda) abused to execute commands and deploy malicious files, blending malicious activity into legitimate cloud management channels. Internet-exposed non-production environments (UAT/staging/testing) used as entry points, followed by movement to production environments using shared credentials, tokens or network paths. Application codebases reverse-engineered by the threat actor to develop tailored exploits; unauthorized API calls subsequently initiated using altered/modified application packages, defeating controls that assumed only the legitimate client application would call the APIs. IP allow-listing bypassed by originating traffic from whitelisted third-party fetcher IP pools (such as content-acceleration and app-store review fetchers); any Internet user can cause such shared fetcher services to fetch arbitrary URLs. Micro-value test transactions (such as Rs. 1) performed to validate unauthorized fund flows before executing large-value transfers. Merchant settlement APIs of payment aggregators exploited or abused to move funds. Newly published vulnerabilities exploited as soon as they become public, including file-upload and deserialization exploit chains leading to web shells in PHP and Node.js applications. Cryptocurrency exchanges and virtual digital asset service providers targeted, with wallet keys stolen and funds siphoned from cryptocurrency wallets. Large numbers of custom, tailored scripts created on the fly, with functionally identical variants refined in rapid succession; a pattern consistent with AI-generated code and iterative AI-assisted development. Recommended Actions Treat this campaign as active and escalating: maintain heightened 24x7 security monitoring, with increased staffing and lowered alert thresholds during holidays, weekends and other low-coverage windows. After any incident, assume persistence: perform full eradication with forensic verification and continue periodic threat hunting; entities have been re-attacked after incomplete remediation. Enable centralized, real-time monitoring of cloud audit logs with alerting on high-risk events such as remote command execution, serverless function code updates and creation of roles, users or access keys. Restrict cloud management and serverless execution to approved principals and accounts; alert on any interactive remote-management session or serverless function code change in production. Enforce instance metadata service protections and least-privilege roles for instances and functions; deny wildcard egress in security groups; configure serverless functions with no Internet egress by default. Isolate UAT/staging/testing environments from production - no shared credentials, tokens, API keys, databases or direct network paths and apply production-grade hardening and monitoring to internet-facing non-production environments. Alert on and investigate any access from non-production systems to production systems, credentials or data. Make application deployment directories read-only for the application runtime user; deploy file-integrity monitoring on application directories for web shell detection. Treat client applications and packages as untrusted: enforce server-side validation of every transaction and business rule; implement API request signing with nonce and timestamp; adopt app attestation services and certificate pinning to detect altered or repackaged applications. Establish a rapid patching SLA for internet-facing applications, prioritizing file-upload and deserialization weaknesses in PHP and Node.js applications; use WAF virtual patching as an interim control. Prohibit hardcoded tokens and credentials in source and build code; deploy automated secret scanning across repositories and CI/CD pipelines; use short-lived, fine-grained, least-privileged access tokens and rotate all build and deployment tokens. Alert on token usage from unusual source IPs, user agents or geographies; enforce branch protection, commit signing and mandatory code review on production deployment branches. Replace IP allow-listing of shared third-party fetcher pools with identity-based controls such as mutual TLS, cryptographically signed requests or scoped API keys on dedicated vendor endpoints. Enforce default-deny egress from server segments through allow-listed proxies; unrestricted HTTPS egress was used for command-and-control and data exfiltration. Deploy TLS inspection with alerting on self-signed certificates presented over non-standard ports. Extend real-time transaction monitoring to flag micro-value test transactions to new beneficiaries followed by high-value transactions; treat this pattern as a strong precursor of unauthorized fund transfer and hold or review such flows. Implement transaction velocity rules, new-beneficiary cooling periods and amount-band anomaly detection across all payment and disbursement paths. Enforce server-side validation, maker-checker approval and reconciliation for all merchant settlement instructions submitted through payment aggregator APIs. Store cryptocurrency wallet keys in hardware security modules or cold custody; require multi-signature approvals for withdrawals; monitor withdrawal patterns for anomalies and rotate keys immediately upon any suspected compromise. Prohibit installation or execution of unauthorized security and attack tools including publicly available AI-driven offensive frameworks on corporate infrastructure; monitor for their download and for AI coding-agent processes running with permission checks disabled. Monitor and govern LLM API usage and keys; LLM API traffic originating from servers or other non-development hosts may indicate an attack rig or planted operator console. Establish a policy requiring written approval, defined scope and a time window for all penetration testing; the tools themselves do not validate authorization. Tune SIEM correlation for machine-speed, multi-technique attack patterns , multiple tools and techniques, parallel attack threads, adaptive payload mutation and continuous non-business-hours operation against a single target and adopt automated (SOAR-based) containment. Deploy deception measures such as honeypots, decoy administrative panels and canary credentials; autonomous attack agents enumerate targets exhaustively and are likely to touch decoy assets, generating high-confidence early alerts. Monitor web roots, temporary directories and staging paths for bursts of newly created commented scripts and rapid successive variants of functionally identical scripts - a strong indicator of AI-generated attack tooling. Adopt zero-trust principles , micro-segmentation, identity-based access for every user and service, and inspection of east-west traffic operating on the assumption that the threat actor is already inside the environment. Upon detection of suspicious activity: isolate affected hosts, preserve forensic evidence and logs, rotate all credentials, and report to CERT-In/CSIRT-Fin at incident@cert-in.org.in . Conclusion Entities are advised to report any signs of suspicious activity related to the \"CRAFTY FALCON\" campaign to CERT-In/CSIRT-Fin at incident@cert-in.org.in , along with all relevant logs, at the earliest. Entities shall also contact Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C) for reporting of such fraudulent transactions in bulk at Cyber Fraud Mitigation Centre (CFCFRMS Portal).
